inputs.abstract:
This draft extends an overview and hierarchy of graph parameters by defining
ten further parameters:

- Boxicity
- c-closure
- Chordal intersection dimension
- Cochromatic number
- Distance to block graphs
- Distance to chordal graphs
- Distance to distance-hereditary graphs
- Distance to interval graphs
- Edge clique cover number
- Vertex integrity

Throughout, graphs are finite, simple, and undirected, and may be disconnected.
All ten parameters assign zero to the empty graph. Boxicity and chordal
intersection dimension allow zero dimensions and zero factors, respectively,
so complete graphs have value zero. The c-closure convention also assigns
zero to complete graphs.

The draft also defines the underlying structures and graph classes in
separate concepts:

- Edge clique covers
- Cochromatic partitions
- Box representations
- Interval representations
- Chordal intersection representations
- c-closed graphs
- Chordal graphs
- Block graphs
- Distance-hereditary graphs
- Interval graphs

concepts.title: Block graphs
concepts.description:
A block graph is a graph with no induced cycle of length at least four
and no induced diamond (a complete four-vertex graph minus one edge).
Equivalently, every block is a clique. Empty and disconnected graphs are allowed.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.ChordalGraphs

/-!
---
title: Block graphs
type: definition
---
A block graph is a graph with no induced cycle of length at least four
and no induced diamond (a complete four-vertex graph minus one edge).
Equivalently, every block is a clique. Empty and disconnected graphs are allowed.
-/

namespace Lax560391.BlockGraphs

open Lax560391.ChordalGraphs

/-- The four vertices induce a diamond, `K₄` with edge `cd` removed. -/
def IsInducedDiamond {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) (a b c d : V) : Prop :=
  ([a, b, c, d] : List V).Nodup ∧
  G.Adj a b ∧ G.Adj a c ∧ G.Adj a d ∧
  G.Adj b c ∧ G.Adj b d ∧ ¬ G.Adj c d

/-- Block graphs are the chordal, diamond-free graphs. -/
def IsBlock {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  IsChordal G ∧ ¬ ∃ a b c d : V, IsInducedDiamond G a b c d

end Lax560391.BlockGraphs

concepts.title: Boxicity
concepts.description:
Boxicity is the minimum number of coordinates in an intersection
representation by nonempty axis-parallel closed boxes. Zero coordinates give a
complete graph, so complete graphs have value zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.BoxRepresentation
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Boxicity
type: definition
---
Boxicity is the minimum number of coordinates in an intersection
representation by nonempty axis-parallel closed boxes. Zero coordinates give a
complete graph, so complete graphs have value zero.
-/

namespace Lax560391.Boxicity

/-- An intersection representation by nonempty closed `k`-dimensional
axis-parallel boxes. -/
def HasBoxicityAtMost {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Lax560391.BoxRepresentation.BoxRepresentation G k)

noncomputable def boxicity {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasBoxicityAtMost G k}

end Lax560391.Boxicity

concepts.title: Box representations
concepts.description:
A box representation assigns a nonempty closed axis-parallel real box to
each vertex, with adjacency exactly when the boxes intersect. The dimension
may be zero, in which case the represented graph is complete.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

/-!
---
title: Box representations
type: definition
---
A box representation assigns a nonempty closed axis-parallel real box to
each vertex, with adjacency exactly when the boxes intersect. The dimension
may be zero, in which case the represented graph is complete.
-/

namespace Lax560391.BoxRepresentation

structure BoxRepresentation {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) where
  lo : V → Fin k → ℝ
  hi : V → Fin k → ℝ
  nonempty : ∀ v i, lo v i ≤ hi v i
  represents : ∀ u v, u ≠ v →
    (G.Adj u v ↔ ∀ i, lo u i ≤ hi v i ∧ lo v i ≤ hi u i)

end Lax560391.BoxRepresentation

concepts.title: c-closed graphs
concepts.description:
A graph is c-closed if every pair of distinct nonadjacent vertices has
fewer than c common neighbors. The value c may be zero; exactly the
complete graphs are 0-closed.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card

/-!
---
title: c-closed graphs
type: definition
---
A graph is c-closed if every pair of distinct nonadjacent vertices has
fewer than c common neighbors. The value c may be zero; exactly the
complete graphs are 0-closed.
-/

namespace Lax560391.CClosedGraphs

def IsCClosed {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (c : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ u v : V, u ≠ v → ¬G.Adj u v →
    {w : V | G.Adj u w ∧ G.Adj v w}.ncard < c

end Lax560391.CClosedGraphs

concepts.title: Chordal graphs
concepts.description:
A graph is chordal if it has no induced cycle of length at least four.
Empty and disconnected graphs are allowed.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic

/-!
---
title: Chordal graphs
type: definition
---
A graph is chordal if it has no induced cycle of length at least four.
Empty and disconnected graphs are allowed.
-/

namespace Lax560391.ChordalGraphs

/-- The next vertex index, wrapping from the last index to zero. -/
def cyclicSucc (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (i : Fin n) : Fin n :=
  ⟨(i.val + 1) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩

/-- A chordless cycle of length at least four. -/
def HasInducedLongCycle {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∃ n : ℕ, ∃ hn : 4 ≤ n,
    let next := cyclicSucc n (lt_of_lt_of_le (by decide : 0 < 4) hn)
    ∃ f : Fin n ↪ V,
    (∀ i : Fin n, G.Adj (f i) (f (next i))) ∧
    (∀ i j : Fin n, i ≠ j → j ≠ next i → i ≠ next j →
      ¬ G.Adj (f i) (f j))

/-- No induced cycle of length at least four. -/
def IsChordal {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ¬ HasInducedLongCycle G

end Lax560391.ChordalGraphs

concepts.title: Chordal intersection dimension
concepts.description:
The minimum number of chordal supergraphs whose edge intersection is the
graph. The intersection of zero factors is complete, so complete graphs have
value zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.ChordalIntersectionRepresentation
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Chordal intersection dimension
type: definition
---
The minimum number of chordal supergraphs whose edge intersection is the
graph. The intersection of zero factors is complete, so complete graphs have
value zero.
-/

namespace Lax560391.ChordalIntersectionDimension

/-- `G` is the intersection of `k` chordal graphs on the same vertices.
The distinctness guard gives the intersection of zero graphs the complete
graph rather than a reflexive relation. -/
def HasChordalIntersectionDimensionAtMost {V : Type}
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Lax560391.ChordalIntersectionRepresentation.ChordalIntersectionRepresentation G k)

noncomputable def chordalIntersectionDimension
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasChordalIntersectionDimensionAtMost G k}

end Lax560391.ChordalIntersectionDimension

concepts.title: Chordal intersection representations
concepts.description:
A chordal intersection representation is an indexed family of chordal
graphs on the same vertex set whose edge intersection is the represented
graph. Each factor is consequently a supergraph. Zero factors represent
the complete simple graph.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.ChordalGraphs

/-!
---
title: Chordal intersection representations
type: definition
---
A chordal intersection representation is an indexed family of chordal
graphs on the same vertex set whose edge intersection is the represented
graph. Each factor is consequently a supergraph. Zero factors represent
the complete simple graph.
-/

namespace Lax560391.ChordalIntersectionRepresentation

structure ChordalIntersectionRepresentation {V : Type}
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) where
  factors : Fin k → SimpleGraph V
  chordal : ∀ i, Lax560391.ChordalGraphs.IsChordal (factors i)
  represents : ∀ u v, u ≠ v → (G.Adj u v ↔ ∀ i, (factors i).Adj u v)

end Lax560391.ChordalIntersectionRepresentation

concepts.title: c-closure
concepts.description:
The c-closure is the least natural number c for which the graph is c-closed.
Complete graphs have value zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.CClosedGraphs
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: c-closure
type: definition
---
The c-closure is the least natural number c for which the graph is c-closed.
Complete graphs have value zero.
-/

namespace Lax560391.Closure

noncomputable def closure {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {c : ℕ | Lax560391.CClosedGraphs.IsCClosed G c}

end Lax560391.Closure

concepts.title: Cochromatic number
concepts.description:
The cochromatic number is the least number of parts in a vertex partition
where each part induces either a clique or an independent set. Parts need not
be graph modules. The empty graph has cochromatic number zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.CochromaticPartition
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Cochromatic number
type: definition
---
The cochromatic number is the least number of parts in a vertex partition
where each part induces either a clique or an independent set. Parts need not
be graph modules. The empty graph has cochromatic number zero.
-/

namespace Lax560391.CochromaticNumber

/-- A partition into at most `k` cliques or independent sets. Empty labels
are allowed and do not affect the minimum. -/
def HasCochromaticNumberAtMost {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Lax560391.CochromaticPartition.CochromaticPartition G k)

noncomputable def cochromaticNumber {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasCochromaticNumberAtMost G k}

end Lax560391.CochromaticNumber

concepts.title: Cochromatic partitions
concepts.description:
A cochromatic partition assigns each vertex a part, each part inducing
either a clique or an independent set. Empty labels are allowed. Parts need
not be modules.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic

/-!
---
title: Cochromatic partitions
type: definition
---
A cochromatic partition assigns each vertex a part, each part inducing
either a clique or an independent set. Empty labels are allowed. Parts need
not be modules.
-/

namespace Lax560391.CochromaticPartition

structure CochromaticPartition {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) where
  part : V → Fin k
  homogeneous : ∀ i,
    (∀ u v, u ≠ v → part u = i → part v = i → G.Adj u v) ∨
    (∀ u v, part u = i → part v = i → ¬ G.Adj u v)

end Lax560391.CochromaticPartition

concepts.title: Distance-hereditary graphs
concepts.description:
A graph is distance-hereditary if every connected induced subgraph preserves
the distances between its vertices. Extended shortest-path distance is used
to distinguish disconnected pairs. Empty and disconnected graphs are allowed.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Metric

/-!
---
title: Distance-hereditary graphs
type: definition
---
A graph is distance-hereditary if every connected induced subgraph preserves
the distances between its vertices. Extended shortest-path distance is used
to distinguish disconnected pairs. Empty and disconnected graphs are allowed.
-/

namespace Lax560391.DistanceHereditaryGraphs

/-- Every connected induced subgraph retains the distances of `G`.
Extended distance avoids identifying disconnected pairs with distance zero. -/
def IsDistanceHereditary {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set V, (G.induce S).Connected →
    ∀ u v : S, (G.induce S).edist u v = G.edist u.1 v.1

end Lax560391.DistanceHereditaryGraphs

concepts.title: Distance to block graphs
concepts.description:
The minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves a block graph, expressed
as a chordal graph with no induced diamond.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.BlockGraphs
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Distance to block graphs
type: definition
---
The minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves a block graph, expressed
as a chordal graph with no induced diamond.
-/

namespace Lax560391.DistanceToBlock

open Lax560391.BlockGraphs

noncomputable def distanceToBlock {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | ∃ S : Finset V, (S.card = k) ∧
    (IsBlock (G.induce {v | v ∉ S}))}

end Lax560391.DistanceToBlock

concepts.title: Distance to chordal graphs
concepts.description:
The minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves a graph with no induced
cycle of length at least four.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.ChordalGraphs
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Distance to chordal graphs
type: definition
---
The minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves a graph with no induced
cycle of length at least four.
-/

namespace Lax560391.DistanceToChordal

open Lax560391.ChordalGraphs

noncomputable def distanceToChordal {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | ∃ S : Finset V, (S.card = k) ∧
    (IsChordal (G.induce {v | v ∉ S}))}

end Lax560391.DistanceToChordal

concepts.title: Distance to distance-hereditary graphs
concepts.description:
The minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves a graph in which every
connected induced subgraph preserves distances.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.DistanceHereditaryGraphs
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Distance to distance-hereditary graphs
type: definition
---
The minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves a graph in which every
connected induced subgraph preserves distances.
-/

namespace Lax560391.DistanceToDistanceHereditary

open Lax560391.DistanceHereditaryGraphs

noncomputable def distanceToDistanceHereditary
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k : ℕ | ∃ S : Finset V, (S.card = k) ∧

concepts.title: Distance to interval graphs
concepts.description:
The minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves an intersection graph of
nonempty closed intervals on the real line.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.IntervalGraphs
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Distance to interval graphs
type: definition
---
The minimum number of vertices whose deletion leaves an intersection graph of
nonempty closed intervals on the real line.
-/

open Lax560391.IntervalGraphs

concepts.title: Edge clique cover number
concepts.description:
An edge clique cover is a family of vertex cliques such that every graph edge
has both endpoints in at least one family member. Its number is the minimum
size of such a family. An edgeless graph has edge clique cover number zero.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.EdgeCliqueCovering
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Edge clique cover number
type: definition
---
An edge clique cover is a family of vertex cliques such that every graph edge
has both endpoints in at least one family member. Its number is the minimum
size of such a family. An edgeless graph has edge clique cover number zero.
-/

namespace Lax560391.EdgeCliqueCover

/-- `k` indexed cliques cover every edge of `G`. Repeated or empty cliques
are harmless because the minimum index count is taken. -/
def HasEdgeCliqueCoverAtMost {V : Type} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Lax560391.EdgeCliqueCovering.EdgeCliqueCovering G k)

noncomputable def edgeCliqueCover {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasEdgeCliqueCoverAtMost G k}

end Lax560391.EdgeCliqueCover

concepts.title: Edge clique covers
concepts.description:
An edge clique cover is an indexed family of vertex cliques covering every
edge. Cliques may overlap, be empty, or repeat; isolated vertices need not
be covered.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique

/-!
---
title: Edge clique covers
type: definition
---
An edge clique cover is an indexed family of vertex cliques covering every
edge. Cliques may overlap, be empty, or repeat; isolated vertices need not
be covered.
-/

namespace Lax560391.EdgeCliqueCovering

structure EdgeCliqueCovering {V : Type} [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) where
  cliques : Fin k → Finset V
  isClique : ∀ i, ∀ u ∈ cliques i, ∀ v ∈ cliques i, u ≠ v → G.Adj u v
  covers : ∀ ⦃u v⦄, G.Adj u v → ∃ i, u ∈ cliques i ∧ v ∈ cliques i

end Lax560391.EdgeCliqueCovering

concepts.title: Interval graphs
concepts.description:
An interval graph is a graph admitting an interval representation by
nonempty closed real intervals. Empty and disconnected graphs are allowed.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax560391.IntervalRepresentation

/-!
---
title: Interval graphs
type: definition
---
An interval graph is a graph admitting an interval representation by
nonempty closed real intervals. Empty and disconnected graphs are allowed.
-/

namespace Lax560391.IntervalGraphs

def IsInterval {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (Lax560391.IntervalRepresentation.IntervalRepresentation G)

end Lax560391.IntervalGraphs

concepts.title: Interval representations
concepts.description:
An interval representation assigns a nonempty closed real interval to each
vertex, with adjacency exactly when two distinct vertices have intersecting
intervals. Point intervals and repeated intervals are allowed.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic

/-!
---
title: Interval representations
type: definition
---
An interval representation assigns a nonempty closed real interval to each
vertex, with adjacency exactly when two distinct vertices have intersecting
intervals. Point intervals and repeated intervals are allowed.
-/

namespace Lax560391.IntervalRepresentation

structure IntervalRepresentation {V : Type} (G : SimpleGraph V) where
  lo : V → ℝ
  hi : V → ℝ
  nonempty : ∀ v, lo v ≤ hi v
  represents : ∀ u v, u ≠ v →
    (G.Adj u v ↔ lo u ≤ hi v ∧ lo v ≤ hi u)

end Lax560391.IntervalRepresentation

concepts.title: Vertex integrity
concepts.description:
The vertex integrity of a finite graph is the minimum, over vertex sets `S`,
of the size of `S` plus the order of the largest connected component of the
graph induced by the remaining vertices. The maximum component order is zero
when no vertices remain.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Connectivity.Connected
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Mathlib.Order.Lattice.Nat

/-!
---
title: Vertex integrity
type: definition
---
The vertex integrity of a finite graph is the minimum, over vertex sets `S`,
of the size of `S` plus the order of the largest connected component of the
graph induced by the remaining vertices. The maximum component order is zero
when no vertices remain.
-/

namespace Lax560391.VertexIntegrity

/-- Deleting `S` leaves no component larger than `k - |S|`. -/
def HasVertexIntegrityAtMost {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ S : Set V, S.ncard ≤ k ∧
    ∀ C : (G.induce Sᶜ).ConnectedComponent,
      S.ncard + C.supp.ncard ≤ k

/-- The minimum of deletion-set size plus largest remaining component size. -/
noncomputable def vertexIntegrity {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  sInf {k | HasVertexIntegrityAtMost G k}

end Lax560391.VertexIntegrity
